name: steel-hammering-epic
prompt: Low heroic camera angle, close to the anvil and looking slightly upward so the anvil and the smith's arms tower over the frame. The dark stone interior of a great blacksmith's forge at night: soot-blackened brick, heavy timber beams, the far walls lost in blackness, a deep orange hearth burning behind. A sword blade heated to glowing orange-white along its length lies across a heavy black iron anvil, gripped in long iron tongs. A big blacksmith's hammer swings down through a slow powerful arc and strikes the hot steel. On the impact a dense burst of white-hot sparks explodes outward toward the camera and arcs downward under gravity, scattering and dying as they fall; the struck metal flares yellow-white at the point of contact and dims again; the hammer rebounds off the steel, rises, and comes down for the next blow in a steady rhythm. Only the smith's gloved hands and bare forearms are in frame, no face and no full body. Shot on 65mm Kodak Vision3 500T film at T2.8, the only light coming from the glowing steel and the hearth, deep black shadow, high dynamic range, visible film grain, natural halation on the hot metal, sparks in sharp focus with slight motion blur on the hammer head. Real documentary footage of a working forge. Epic, monumental, heroic scale.
